title: Your $5 Coffee Has a Hidden 8-Cent Fee #Shorts
description:
You tap your card, it beeps, and your coffee is approved in about two seconds. But that beep sends a message through a processor, a card network, and your bank, and "approved" is only a promise: the real money lands one to three days later, minus fees. On a $5 coffee that is about 8 cents, and across America it adds up to $198 billion a year that everyone pays through prices, even cash buyers.

Watch the full trip: What Happens in the 2 Seconds After You Tap Your Card https://youtu.be/49dFN07-QQo

Sources:
[S1] Stripe, Card authorization explained: https://stripe.com/resources/more/card-authorization-explained
[S4] Congressional Research Service, Merchant Discount, Interchange, and Other Transaction Fees in the Retail Electronic Payment System (IF11893, 2021): https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/IF11893.html
[S5] Nilson Report, Merchant processing fees in the United States 2025: https://nilsonreport.com/articles/merchant-processing-fees-in-the-united-states-2025/
[S6] Stripe, Payment settlement explained: https://stripe.com/resources/more/payment-settlement-explained-how-it-works-and-how-long-it-takes

Our own calculation:
[D1] $5.00 x 1.59% (average U.S. merchant fee rate, 2025) = 7.95 cents, about 8 cents. This is a national average; real fees vary by card, merchant, and sale size.
